title: Implement server-session logout
verify: Logout revokes the server session, clears the session cookie, redirects to /login, and denies reuse of the captured session token.
Logout reuses the accepted Authentication Transport boundary and does not own navigation shell rendering.
evidence_required: authentication-transport.md#session-issuance-and-revocation RED: logout only clears browser state or leaves the server session usable; GREEN: isolated route tests prove revocation, cookie clearing, redirect, and old-session denial without changing unrelated sessions; artifact: .tasks/TASK-061-T3-FT-007-W28/ and .protocols/TASK-061-T3-FT-007-W28/.
purpose: Keep logout server-authoritative and independently verifiable from the navigation shell.
success_outcome: A logout request invalidates the server session and returns the browser to login without changing unrelated account data.
anti_goals: Do not implement the common navigation shell.
Do not add a client-only logout path or new session authority.
Do not use study-calendar.db in tests.
constraints: Identity & Access owns session revocation and cookie semantics.
The focused integration proof is owned by TASK-062; this task proves only the logout unit.
Tests use isolated disposable state and never the shared real database.
invariants: The captured session cannot authorize a protected request after logout.
Unrelated sessions and account/profile facts are unchanged.
No client-supplied actor or role controls revocation.
verification_targets: authentication-transport.md#session-issuance-and-revocation: server-session, cookie, redirect, and old-token matrix.
access-control.md#binding-and-session-rules: session authority remains in Identity & Access.

stop_conditions: Stop if logout requires a new session lifecycle or client-only authority.
Stop if proving logout requires changing the common shell or unrelated provider modules.
